stem: A breeder selects one exceptional plant from a highly variable F2 family and concludes that its desirable phenotype will breed true in the next generation. Which evaluation is strongest?
choices: The conclusion is justified because F2 individuals are genetically fixed
The conclusion is weak because segregation, recombination and parental heterozygosity can produce non-breeding-true individuals; progeny evidence is needed
The conclusion is justified if the plant was the largest in the family
The conclusion is weak only if the cultivar name changed
rationale: An individual phenotype does not establish breeding value or fixation in a segregating population. Progeny testing and pedigree evidence are needed to evaluate inheritance.
